summary: Grant/Baker County, OR: 43-ft platform in the 1920s, 41-ft tower from 1949, emergency use in the 1960s, demolished 1986; no source describes remains.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com give a 43-foot platform from the 1920s and a 22-foot tower in 1934. Forest Lookouts gives the platform as 45 feet, describes a lookout station still to be built in 1937, and does not mention a 1934 tower. The record keeps the 1934 event from the two register-style sources; the story reports the disagreement.

The register calls the 1949 structure a 41-foot treated timber L-4 tower; Forest Lookouts calls it a 41-foot CT-2 tower with a 14 by 14 foot house. Both give 41 feet, so the record uses the common height and house size.
firelookout.com lists Patti Trimble in 1968; Forest Lookouts dates her to September 1967. The record uses the newspaper date.

notes_for_editor: Three sources agree on the 1949 tower and the emergency use, but they disagree on the early dates. Forest Lookouts (1937 note) argues against the 1934 tower that the register and firelookout.com give, so the 1934 event is flagged for review. Forest Lookouts spells the point 'Poque Point' in one 1937 item; the record uses the standard name. The Unity Ranger Station (Wikipedia, not cited) has a separate fire lookout tower built 1936-38; it is not this site and should not be confused with it. No source describes the site today, and access is omitted because no source describes it. No photos added because no image URLs were captured.
